questions.prompt: Which element creates a hyperlink to another page?
questions.explanation: The anchor element <a> with an href attribute creates hyperlinks; <link> is for external resources such as stylesheets.

questions.prompt: Which attribute provides alternative text for an element?
questions.explanation: The alt attribute gives text used by screen readers and shown if the image fails to load.

questions.prompt: Which element defines an unordered (bulleted) list?
questions.explanation: <ul> is an unordered list; <ol> is ordered and <li> is a list item.

questions.prompt: Which element wraps all the visible content of an HTML document?
questions.explanation: <body> holds the visible content; <head> holds metadata such as the title and links.

questions.prompt: What does the <!DOCTYPE html> declaration do?
options: Tells the browser to render the page in standards mode as HTML5
Links the page to a stylesheet
questions.explanation: The doctype prevents quirks mode so the browser uses standards-compliant rendering.

questions.prompt: Which input type hides the characters the user types?
questions.explanation: type="password" obscures the typed characters; type="hidden" is simply not displayed at all.

questions.prompt: Which element inserts a single line break?
questions.explanation: is a void element that produces a line break.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of <label for="email">?
options: It sets the name submitted for the input
It links the input to a stylesheet
It associates the label with the control whose id is "email", so clicking the label focuses the control
questions.explanation: The for attribute references the control's id, improving usability and accessibility.

questions.prompt: Which attribute prevents a form from submitting when a field is left empty?
questions.explanation: The boolean required attribute triggers built-in constraint validation.

questions.prompt: What is the main difference between <section> and <div>?
options: <section> has semantic meaning as a thematic grouping, while <div> has none
questions.explanation: <div> is a generic container; <section> conveys a thematic group of content, usually with a heading.

questions.prompt: Which element best represents self-contained content that could be distributed independently, such as a blog post?
questions.explanation: <article> is for self-contained, independently distributable content.

questions.prompt: What does the defer attribute on an external <script> do?
options: Runs the script only after the page fully loads and images finish
Prevents the script from ever running
Runs the script before any HTML is parsed
Downloads the script in parallel and runs it after the document is parsed, preserving order
questions.explanation: Deferred scripts execute after parsing, before DOMContentLoaded, in document order.

questions.prompt: Which attribute makes the browser delay loading an off-screen image until it is near the viewport?
questions.explanation: loading="lazy" on enables native lazy loading.

questions.prompt: What does <th scope="col"> communicate?
options: The cell is sorted by column
The cell is a header for the cells below it in its column
The cell is hidden from screen readers
questions.explanation: scope tells assistive technology which cells a header applies to.

questions.prompt: Why is <button> preferred over <div role="button" onclick="...">?
options: The div cannot receive click events
A button is always styled better
A native button is focusable and activates with Enter and Space by default; the div needs extra tabindex and key handling
questions.explanation: Native elements come with built-in semantics, focus and keyboard behavior that ARIA roles alone do not provide.

questions.prompt: What problem does aria-hidden="true" cause on a focusable element such as a link?
options: It stops the link from navigating
The element is removed from the accessibility tree yet still receives keyboard focus, leaving users on something unannounced
questions.explanation: aria-hidden affects only assistive technology exposure, not focusability or visibility.

questions.prompt: What does alt="" on an signal?
options: The image is missing and invalid
The screen reader should read the file name
The image should be lazy loaded
The image is decorative and should be skipped by screen readers
questions.explanation: An empty alt marks decorative images; omitting alt entirely may cause the file name to be announced.

questions.prompt: What is the role of the sizes attribute alongside srcset with width descriptors?
options: It tells the browser the image's rendered layout width so it can choose the best candidate before layout completes
It sets the image's file size limit
It forces the browser to download all candidates
It defines the image's intrinsic resolution
questions.explanation: Without sizes the browser assumes 100vw; sizes lets it pick an appropriate source from srcset.

questions.prompt: Which heading practice is correct for accessibility?
options: Choose levels by desired font size
Choose heading levels to reflect document structure without skipping levels, and style size with CSS
Use <b> instead of headings for subsections
questions.explanation: Headings form an outline used for navigation; visual size should come from CSS.

questions.prompt: How does <script type="module"> differ in loading behavior from a classic script?
options: It blocks parsing until it runs
It runs only in the head
It is deferred by default and executes in strict mode with its own module scope
It shares variables globally with every script
questions.explanation: Module scripts are deferred automatically, strict, and scoped to the module.

questions.prompt: What happens when a <dialog> is opened with showModal()?
options: It opens non-blocking while the page stays interactive
It is placed in the top layer, the rest of the page becomes inert, and Escape closes it
It requires the open attribute to be set manually
questions.explanation: showModal() makes a modal dialog; show() opens a non-modal one.
